q: How do I make a faceless YouTube video with stock clips, an AI voice and captions?
a: 1. Write the script; Text to Speech (`tts.create`) makes the narration clip (Natural voices are a one-time download; the built-in voice needs none). 2. Lay stock B-roll on V1 to match each line, matching their grade to one look. 3. Music typed Music with Ducking under the narration. 4. Captions from the transcript (`transcript.createCaptions`), styled big. 5. Loudness about −14 LUFS. Check every stock clip's licence.

q: AI voice sounds flat in my faceless video
a: Change pitch and pace in the Text to Speech panel, split long sentences into separate narration clips with small pauses, or record your own voice for the key lines; text to speech has little control over emphasis.

q: Edit a line of the AI narration without redoing everything.
a: Select the narration clip and edit its text (`tts.edit`): it keeps its place and length (trim the end out if the new line is longer); the old version stays so Undo is exact.

q: Edit a church service recorded on two cameras with hymn lyrics on screen.
a: 1. Sync the cameras and the desk audio by waveform, make a multicam and cut live between angles. 2. Desk audio as the main sound, Clean Up Voice on the speaker parts. 3. Lyrics as captions or text graphics timed to the singing (markers on each line help), big and inside the safe area. 4. Chapters for readings, sermon and songs.

q: the speaker's mic is quiet and the singing is loud
a: Even it out: clip gain or Volume keyframes per section, Dynamics on the speaker parts, a limiter on the Mix for the loud singing; aim for steady loudness throughout.

q: Remove the long gaps between parts of the service.
a: Find them in the transcript or by marking the waveform, cut them (Remove Pauses with a long minimum, or by hand) and put short dissolves or audio crossfades on the cuts.

q: Opening credits over the first scene of my short film.
a: Names as text graphics on a track above the footage, one card every few seconds, each held long enough to read twice, in a consistent position and type style; gentle fades in and out. A template with the name and role editable keeps them identical. Leave the important action clear of the text.

q: credits that appear on objects in the scene, like on a wall
a: Pin each name onto a surface with Corner Pin and Track Surface (`tracking.cornerPin`) and a blend mode so it sits on the texture; or attach small titles to a track (`tracking.attach`).

q: Credits are hard to read over a busy background.
a: Add a soft shadow or stroke to the text (`graphics.set`), or a shape behind pinned to the text, or darken the area with a soft window; thin fonts flicker after compression.

q: The old music-player ad look: black dancer silhouette on a bright colour background.
a: Shoot the dancer on green (or against a bright, even background). Key with Ultra Key, then make the dancer solid black (Lumetri Exposure / the node grader's Gain all the way down, or Brightness & Contrast); a bright Color Matte below as the background. Cut the colour changes to the beat.

q: silhouette edges look jagged
a: Clean the key: Choke a little, Soften the edge, check the matte with Output ▸ Alpha Channel; fast moves need a faster shutter at the shoot to avoid blur.

q: Change the background colour on every beat.
a: Several Color Mattes in different colours cut end to end on V1 at the beat markers (`markers.add`, Snap), the keyed silhouette above.

q: A year-in-review video from hundreds of clips and photos.
a: 1. Selects per month (markers, subclips, a bin per month). 2. A song or two fitted with Remix, cut on phrases. 3. A month title card from a template at each section. 4. Photos with slow Scale moves, phone clips matched in grade. 5. Keep each moment short; the best ones get a few extra seconds.

q: mixed vertical phone clips and horizontal camera clips
a: In a 16:9 sequence, vertical clips get a blurred, enlarged copy behind them (Fill frame + Gaussian Blur) with the original on top (Fit to frame); or make a vertical version for socials too.

q: Counter showing the month as the video plays.
a: A small text graphic per month section ('January'…), from a template, placed at each section start; there's no automatic date counter.

q: POV shot where the character gets dizzy and the picture swims.
a: Stack effects and keyframe them up as it gets worse: Wave Warp or Turbulent Displace for the wobble, Echo for double vision, a little Gaussian Blur, Wiggle for drifting; muffle the sound with an EQ cutting the highs.

q: double vision effect
a: A copy of the clip above, slightly offset (Motion Position) at about 50 % Opacity, its offset keyframed to drift apart and back; or Echo with a short Echo Time.

q: Character faints: vision blurs, darkens and goes black.
a: Keyframe Gaussian Blur up, a vignette closing in (an inverted soft window with Gain down, or Lumetri Vignette Amount), then fade to black; the sound muffles and fades at the same time.

q: A big word fills the screen and the next shot appears inside it, then takes over.
a: Track Matte Key: the next shot on a track above the current one, using the title as its matte (Composite Using alpha), so it shows only inside the letters; turn the title track's output off (`timeline.setTrack`, enabled false), since switching the title clip off would remove the matte; keyframe the title's Scale up until it fills the frame, then remove the matte (cut to the full shot).

q: word slides across and wipes to the next clip
a: The next clip above with a rectangle mask on Opacity whose edge follows the sliding word (both keyframed together), so the word's edge carries the wipe.

q: Title card that splits open to reveal the scene.
a: Two halves of the title card (two masked copies), each moved off screen with Position keyframes in opposite directions, eased; the scene underneath.

q: Interview recorded on a phone's voice memo app sounds thin and noisy.
a: Clean Up Voice first (`audio.cleanupVoice`), then Clarity: Enhance Speech and an EQ preset (Warm Voice or Balanced Voice) for body; Voice Isolation for background noise. Thin phone audio can't become a studio mic, so stop where it sounds natural.

q: voice memo audio is out of sync with my camera video
a: Synchronize by audio (`clip.synchronize`) using the camera's scratch sound, then check the end: if it drifts (variable frame rate or clock difference), cut and re-sync later sections.

q: Phone audio has clipping distortion on loud laughs.
a: Clipped peaks can't be fully repaired; lower them with Volume keyframes so they stand out less, and cover the worst ones with other audio or cut them.

q: Inspirational quotes over slow B-roll for social media.
a: Calm B-roll on V1 (a little slowed down), a quote graphic on V2 with large readable type, a soft shadow or dark gradient behind for contrast, held long enough to read twice; one template for all quotes with the text and author editable.

q: quote words appearing one at a time
a: Separate text layers or graphics per word or phrase, starting one after another on the timeline with short Opacity fades; or per-character styles keyed by hand.

q: Square and vertical versions of the quote videos.
a: Duplicate the sequence at 1080 × 1080 and 1080 × 1920, reposition the B-roll (or Auto Reframe), and move the quote into the middle third; queue all exports.

q: Compare two attempts at the same jump by overlaying them semi-transparent.
a: Both clips on V1 and V2, aligned so the take-off happens on the same frame (slip one), the top at about 50 % Opacity (Normal or Difference blend); a locked-off camera makes it readable. Label each with a small text graphic.

q: golf swing comparison: my swing vs a pro side by side and overlaid
a: Side by side: each clip on its own track, Motion Position to its half (a mask crops). Overlaid: the top at 50 % Opacity. Sync both to the moment of impact, and slow them with Speed / Duration (Optical Flow) to study.

q: Freeze both attempts at the key moment with lines drawn.
a: Insert Frame Hold Segment on both at the key frame (`clip.insertFrameHoldSegment`), then shape layers (lines, angles) in a graphic above, animated on.
